title: cheaper way to test-fire without blowing up the stand

messages.content: gary's freaking out about test costs again. how do we test-fire leviathan engines cheapr w/o blowing up the stand?

One approach is to simulate engine conditions more thoroughly before a physical test. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) can model combustion processes to predict behavior without physical risks. We could also develop a modular test setup that isolates components to test individually. This strategy might reduce the risk and cost associated with full-scale tests.
cfd sounds like textbook cowardice. what if we just mass produce engines? then we don't care if a few go boom!

Mass production could indeed reduce per-unit costs, but we also need to consider the logistics of scaling manufacturing and potential bottlenecks. It might be worth investing in rapid prototyping for specific components, allowing quicker iteration without the full-scale risks. This way, we balance testing frequency with reliability.
sounds like slow bureaucracy. is there a way to safely contain an explosion so we just keep testing?

We could explore building robust test chambers with reinforced materials, similar to hardened bunkers, that can withstand high-pressure events. Another idea is water deluge systems to dampen explosive forces during a test, reducing stand damage. But, these solutions involve significant upfront costs, even if they save in the long run.
ok, ok, let's say we just synchronize the tests with fireworks shows. at least gary won't complain about the entertainment value.

That's certainly an innovative way to frame it! In all seriousness, integrating aspects of entertainment doesn't address the core issue of costs and risks. Focusing on precision in simulations and test containment will provide more reliable data while keeping Gary Puddle from losing too much sleep. We can keep iterating on creative solutions!
